lessons.title: Reading About a Famous Inventor
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about a famous toy inventor from a simple biography text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about the inventor.
I can say what they invented.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what an 'inventor' is.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a simple biography extract about a toy inventor (e.g. the creator of Lego or the teddy bear), modelling fact-finding.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer retrieval questions about the inventor's life and invention.

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction/biography retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts learned about the inventor.
lessons.home_link: Ask your family if they know who invented a favourite toy.

lessons.title: Addition to 20 Using a Number Line
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to add two numbers within 20 using a number line.
success_criteria: I can use a number line to add.
I can solve an addition problem within 20.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition within 10 using counters.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model adding using a number line, making jumps forward.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve addition problems within 20 using a number line, recording their jumps.
key_questions: How many jumps did you make?

differentiation.support: Add within 10 using the number line
differentiation.greater_depth: Add within 20 with two-digit + one-digit numbers

lessons.assessment_notes: Record number line addition strategy use — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire number line addition quiz.
lessons.home_link: Practise adding using a number line drawn at home.

lessons.title: Who Invented the Teddy Bear?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe the story of a significant invention.
success_criteria: I can say who is linked to inventing the teddy bear.
I can describe roughly when this happened.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a teddy bear and discuss its history.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Tell the simple story of the teddy bear's origin (linked to Theodore Roosevelt/Morris Michtom), discussing significance.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and sequence the simple story of the teddy bear's invention.
key_questions: Who is linked to the first teddy bear?
Why do you think it became so popular?

differentiation.greater_depth: Retell the story independently with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of a significant historical event/individual — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the teddy bear invention story.
lessons.home_link: Share the teddy bear story with your family.

lessons.title: Designing an Invention Sketch
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sketch and label a design for an invented toy.
success_criteria: I can sketch a toy design.
I can label at least two parts.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap toy design from Week 2.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sketching an invention design with labelled parts, like an inventor's notebook.
lessons.independent_task: Children sketch and label their own invented toy design in an 'inventor's notebook' style.

differentiation.support: Adult supports labelling with word bank
differentiation.greater_depth: Add a written explanation of how it works

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe design sketching and labelling skill — evidence for ART.1/DT links.
lessons.plenary: Share invention sketches with the class.
lessons.home_link: Show your invention sketch to your family and explain it.

lessons.title: Writing About My Own Invention
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences describing their own invented toy.
success_criteria: I can write what my invention does.
I can use a capital letter and full stop.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Monday's invention sketch.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing sentences describing an invention using the sketch as a reference.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing their invented toy from Monday.
key_questions: Can you describe how it works?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with descriptive detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share invention descriptions with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Read your invention description to your family.

lessons.title: Subtraction to 20 Using a Number Line
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to subtract within 20 using a number line.
success_criteria: I can use a number line to subtract.
I can solve a subtraction problem within 20.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap subtraction within 10.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model subtracting using a number line, making jumps backward.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve subtraction problems within 20 using a number line.
key_questions: How many jumps back did you make?

differentiation.support: Subtract within 10 using the number line
differentiation.greater_depth: Subtract within 20 with two-digit numbers

lessons.assessment_notes: Record number line subtraction strategy use — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire number line subtraction quiz.
lessons.home_link: Practise subtracting using a number line drawn at home.

lessons.title: The Inventor of Lego
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe key facts about the invention of Lego.
success_criteria: I can say who invented Lego and roughly when.
I can say why it became popular.
lessons.starter_activity: Play with Lego/building bricks and discuss.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Tell the story of Ole Kirk Christiansen and the invention of Lego, discussing why interlocking bricks were a clever idea.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and record key facts about the invention of Lego.
key_questions: Why do people still love Lego today?

differentiation.greater_depth: Record 4+ facts and explain significance

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of a significant invention's story — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the Lego invention story.
lessons.home_link: Build something with any building bricks at home.

lessons.title: Building Brick Sculpture
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a 3D sculpture using building bricks.
success_criteria: I can build a 3D structure.
I can describe my sculpture.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at examples of Lego sculptures/art.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss building bricks as an art material, showing examples of brick sculptures.
lessons.independent_task: Children build their own free-choice 3D sculpture using building bricks, then describe it.

differentiation.greater_depth: Build a more complex structure and explain design choices

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe 3D construction and spatial skill — evidence for ART.1/MATHS.GEO links.
lessons.plenary: Display sculptures and children describe them.
lessons.home_link: Build a sculpture using any building toys at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Inventor-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words related to inventors and inventions.
success_criteria: I can blend and read invention words.
I can read a sentence about an inventor.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap graphemes practised this term.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending invention-themed words.
lessons.independent_task: Children read invention-themed word and sentence cards.

differentiation.greater_depth: Read sentences independently and fluently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading invention words over the week.

lessons.title: Missing Number Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve missing number addition/subtraction problems within 20.
success_criteria: I can find a missing number in an addition sentence.
I can find a missing number in a subtraction sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction number sentences.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving missing number problems (e.g. 7 + ? = 12) using concrete objects and a number line.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve missing number problems within 20 using their preferred strategy.
key_questions: How did you work it out?

differentiation.greater_depth: Missing numbers within 20 without concrete support

lessons.assessment_notes: Record missing number problem-solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire missing number quiz.
lessons.home_link: Practise missing number problems together at home.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Inventors
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare two toy inventors and their inventions.
success_criteria: I can say one thing that is similar about the two inventors.
I can say one thing that is different.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the two inventors learned about this week (teddy bear, Lego).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing the two inventors' stories and inventions.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a simple comparison chart for the two inventors.
key_questions: What is similar about these inventors?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give 3+ similarities/differences independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative historical thinking — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Share comparisons made with the class.
lessons.home_link: Talk about your favourite inventor learned about this week.

lessons.title: Art Inspired by an Inventor's Notebook
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create artwork inspired by historical inventors' sketchbooks.
success_criteria: I can create a sketchbook-style page.
I can include labelled drawings.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at examples of famous inventors' sketchbooks (e.g. Leonardo da Vinci, simplified).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how inventors used sketchbooks to plan ideas, modelling a simple labelled sketch page.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own 'inventor's sketchbook' page with labelled drawings of toy ideas.
key_questions: What is your sketchbook page about?

differentiation.greater_depth: Include multiple sketches with detailed labels

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe sketchbook-style creative recording — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Share sketchbook pages with the class.
lessons.home_link: Start your own inventor's sketchbook at home.

lessons.title: Hot-Seating a Famous Inventor
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to ask and answer questions in role as a famous inventor.
success_criteria: I can ask a question to the 'inventor'.
I can answer a question in role.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about the inventors learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model hot-seating (adult or a confident child in role as the inventor, answering questions).
lessons.independent_task: In pairs, children take turns hot-seating as an inventor and asking questions.
resources_needed: Simple inventor prop (e.g. hat, name badge)

differentiation.greater_depth: Ask and answer unprompted with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and historical knowledge application — evidence for ENG.SL1/HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap interesting answers given in role.
lessons.home_link: Role-play being an inventor and explain your invention to your family.

lessons.title: Doubling Numbers to 10
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to double numbers up to 10.
success_criteria: I can double a number using counters.
I can recall some doubles facts.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap doubling from EYFS if needed.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model doubling numbers 1-10 using counters and recording as addition (e.g. 4+4=8).
lessons.independent_task: Children practise doubling numbers to 10, recording as addition number sentences.
key_questions: How did you work it out?

differentiation.greater_depth: Recall doubles to 10 without counters

lessons.assessment_notes: Record doubling fluency — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire doubles quiz.
lessons.home_link: Practise doubling small numbers at home.

lessons.title: Would I Like to Be an Inventor?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain what skills an inventor might need.
success_criteria: I can name a skill an inventor needs.
I can say if I'd like to be an inventor and why.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what makes someone a good inventor (creativity, persistence, curiosity).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss inventor skills, linking to growth mindset (trying again if an idea doesn't work).
lessons.independent_task: Children write/draw about whether they'd like to be an inventor and why, naming a skill they have.
key_questions: What skill does an inventor need?
Would you like to be an inventor?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning with multiple skills named

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflective thinking linking history to personal aspiration — evidence for HIST.2/PSHE links.
lessons.plenary: Share reflections with the class.
lessons.home_link: Talk about an idea you have and how you might make it happen.

lessons.title: Making a Prototype Model
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple prototype model of their invented toy.
success_criteria: I can build a simple model of my invention.
I can explain how it works.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap invention sketches from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what a 'prototype' is, modelling building a simple model from craft materials.
lessons.independent_task: Children construct a simple prototype model of their invented toy using craft/junk materials.
key_questions: Does your model match your sketch?

differentiation.greater_depth: Refine and adapt the design during construction

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe design-to-model translation skill — evidence for ART.1/DT links.
lessons.plenary: Display prototype models together.
lessons.home_link: Show your prototype to your family and explain how it works.

lessons.title: Presenting My Invention
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present their invention prototype clearly to the class.
success_criteria: I can explain what my invention does.
I can answer one question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's invention learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation of an invention (what it is, what it does, why it's useful).
lessons.independent_task: Children present their prototype invention to a small group, answering a question.

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language progress — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all inventions presented.
lessons.home_link: Present your invention to your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Addition, Subtraction, Doubling
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply addition, subtraction, and doubling skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can add and subtract within 20.
I can double numbers to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of number line addition/subtraction and doubling.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: number line addition, number line subtraction, doubling.

differentiation.greater_depth: Independent completion with extension challenges

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 6 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N2/N3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising addition, subtraction and doubling over the weekend.

lessons.title: Inventors Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about toy inventors learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name an inventor and their invention.
I can say why their invention was significant.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's history learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about inventors.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Famous Toy Inventors' display combining facts, comparisons, and sketchbook pages from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about inventors?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain multiple ideas with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished 'Famous Toy Inventors' display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about inventors with your family.

lessons.title: Art Celebration: Inventor's Gallery
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present their invention artwork and prototypes as a class gallery.
success_criteria: I can display my invention work.
I can talk about my favourite piece.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all art created this week (sketches, sculptures, sketchbook pages, prototypes).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss arranging work for a class 'Inventor's Gallery'.
lessons.independent_task: Children help set up and present the finished Inventor's Gallery display.
resources_needed: All art/prototype work from the week
key_questions: Which piece are you most proud of?
What did you learn making it?

differentiation.support: Point to work and name what it is
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the design process behind their favourite piece

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflective language and design process recall — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class gallery walk of the Inventor's Gallery.
lessons.home_link: Show your favourite piece from this week to your family.
